spot:tongatapu-1.name: Haʻamonga ʻa Maui
spot:tongatapu-1.bio: A 13th-century coral limestone trilithon near Niutoua, known as the Stonehenge of the Pacific.

spot:tongatapu-2.name: Lapaha
spot:tongatapu-2.bio: Terraced royal tombs from 1200–1800 AD that resemble pyramid bases, with information signs on site.

spot:tongatapu-5.name: Mapu a Vaea
spot:tongatapu-5.bio: Blowholes near Houma where waves driven into the reef shoot water into the air.

spot:tongatapu-7.name: Talamahu Market
spot:tongatapu-7.bio: Nukuʻalofa's main market, with fruit and root crops downstairs and handicrafts and carvings upstairs.

spot:tongatapu-9.name: Pangaimotu
spot:tongatapu-9.bio: A small resort island ten minutes by boat from Nukuʻalofa, with a shipwreck to snorkel around.

spot:vavau-1.name: Swallows Cave
spot:vavau-1.bio: Sea cave at Kapa Island's northwest tip, home to swiftlets and fish schools that snorkellers swim among.

spot:vavau-3.name: Mount Talau
spot:vavau-3.bio: Hill of 131 m above Neiafu, a steep climb to a lookout over the harbour.

spot:vavau-6.name: Neiafu Market
spot:vavau-6.bio: Neiafu's harbourside market for fish, fruit, vegetables and handicrafts, best on Saturday mornings.

spot:vavau-8.name: Tapana Island
spot:vavau-8.bio: Island ten minutes by boat from 'Utu Vava'u with beach fales and a Spanish restaurant.

spot:eua-1.name: ʻEua National Park
spot:eua-1.bio: Tonga's only forest national park, a rainforest strip on the east coast backed by cliffs, caves and chasms.

dest:tongatapu:why1.name: See the Haʻamonga ʻa Maui trilithon

dest:tongatapu:why4.name: Swim in an underground freshwater cave

dest:vavau:why3.name: Snorkel and swim into sea caves

dest:vavau:why4.name: Climb to lookouts over the harbour

spot:tongatapu-12.name: Haʻatafu Beach
spot:tongatapu-12.bio: A long white-sand beach lined with palms on the northwest peninsula, with snorkelling and surfing.

spot:tongatapu-13.name: St Mary's Cathedral
spot:tongatapu-13.bio: Seat of Tonga's diocese on Vuna Road in Nukuʻalofa, with two low baroque towers flanking a modern centre.

spot:haapai-1.name: Tofua
spot:haapai-1.bio: Active volcanic island with a steep caldera and a one-hour climb to the crater, reached by hired boat.

spot:haapai-2.name: Kao
spot:haapai-2.bio: Dormant volcanic island rising 1,030 m, the highest point in Tonga, seen from Tofua's crater and by boat.

spot:eua-12.name: Tufuvai Beach
spot:eua-12.bio: A west-coast beach within easy reach of the waterfront accommodation at Tufuvai.

spot:tongatapu-3.name: Hūfangalupe
spot:tongatapu-3.bio: A natural stone land bridge on the south coast with waves crashing into a sinkhole beneath it.

spot:tongatapu-4.name: ʻAnahulu Cave
spot:tongatapu-4.bio: A lit limestone cave about 400 m long with a walkway to a freshwater pool where visitors can swim.

spot:tongatapu-8.name: Malaʻe Kula
spot:tongatapu-8.bio: Nukuʻalofa's cemetery, whose ornate royal family tomb is its most visited sight.

spot:tongatapu-11.name: Keleti Beach
spot:tongatapu-11.bio: A sandy cove with natural blowholes, reached through the former Keleti Beach Resort, with lagoon swimming.

spot:tongatapu-14.name: Fishing Pigs
spot:tongatapu-14.bio: Pigs forage for seafood in the mudflats at Navutoka village, a signposted roadside stop.

spot:vavau-2.name: Mariner's Cave
spot:vavau-2.bio: Cave on Nuapapu Island entered by a 4 m underwater swim, for confident swimmers on day boat tours.

spot:vavau-4.name: Utula'aina Lookout
spot:vavau-4.bio: Clifftop lookout in the north over white beaches and whale-watching water, reached by gravel road.

spot:eua-5.name: Big 'Ovava Tree #1
spot:eua-5.bio: A banyan said to be 800 years old, its roots plunging into the caves below.

spot:eua-8.name: Fangatave Beach
spot:eua-8.bio: A remote northeast beach reached on a guided hike, enclosed by high limestone cliffs.

spot:eua-13.name: Ufilei Beach
spot:eua-13.bio: One of the island's better swimming beaches, just north of 'Ohonua.
